title: Classic Gravlax: Salt, Sugar and Dill Cured Salmon with Mustard-Dill Sauce
summary: A side of salmon cured for 36 hours under salt, sugar, pepper and dill, coated in fresh dill and sliced thinly to serve on rye bread with a sweet mustard-dill sauce.
equipment: deep glass or ceramic dish that fits the fillet

ingredients.item: sashimi-grade salmon fillet, skin on, pin bones removed

ingredients.note: most is rinsed off; see nutrition note

ingredients.item: dill, stalks and all, roughly chopped
dill fronds, finely chopped, for coating

steps.title: Make the cure
steps.text: Stir together the salt, sugar and crushed peppercorns in a small bowl. Equal salt and sugar give a balanced cure: the salt pulls out water and the sugar softens its harshness.

steps.title: Pack the salmon
steps.text: Lay the fillet skin side down on a large double sheet of cling film, with half the chopped dill underneath and half on top. Pack the cure in an even, thick layer over the flesh, then wrap it tightly so the cure stays in contact with the fish.

steps.title: Cure for 36 hours
steps.text: Set the parcel in a deep dish and refrigerate for about 36 h, turning it over once halfway. Brine will leak out as the salt draws moisture from the fish, and the flesh will turn deeper in colour and firm to the touch.

steps.title: Rinse and coat
steps.text: Unwrap the salmon, scrape away the dill and cure and rinse quickly under cold water. Pat it bone dry with kitchen paper, then press the finely chopped dill firmly over the flesh to give a green crust.

steps.title: Whisk the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the mustard, sugar and vinegar together, then add the oil a little at a time, whisking, until the sauce thickens and turns glossy. Stir in the dill; adding the oil slowly helps it emulsify instead of separating.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Hold the long knife almost flat and cut very thin slices on a steep angle down towards the skin, leaving the skin on the board. Arrange the slices on a plate with the rye bread and the mustard-dill sauce.

tips: Partly freezing the cured fillet for 30 min makes very thin slicing much easier.
Ask for a centre-cut piece of even thickness so it cures evenly from end to end.
A common mistake is skipping the drying; damp fish will not hold its dill coating.
safety: RAW NOTE: salt and sugar cure the salmon but do not kill parasites or germs the way heat does. Buy sushi- or sashimi-grade fish from a fishmonger you trust that has been frozen first (-20 °C for 7 days or -35 °C for 15 hours), keep it in the fridge throughout and eat it within 3 days of curing. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
storage: Wrapped tightly, the cured salmon keeps up to 3 days in the fridge. The mustard-dill sauce keeps 1 week covered in the fridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
